newsitem.title: BRAZIL: LatAm stocks seen tied to U.S. Fed upshot this wk.
newsitem.headline: LatAm stocks seen tied to U.S. Fed upshot this wk.

text.p: The trajectory of most Latin American stock exchanges this week hinges on the outcome of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve meeting to weigh a hike in U.S. interest rates, analysts and brokers said.

Although a 25-basis point hike appears to be widely expected, analysts said investors in the region may decide to lay low and remain on the sidelines in a week that will also be slow ahead of Easter holidays.
The exceptions may be Argentina and Chile, where a U.S. interest rate hike apparently has already been factored in, allowing those markets to follow other factors.
Argentine stocks were expected to continue their recovery as a U.S. rate hike has been priced in, dealers said.

"The market should become less volatile and consolidate at slightly higher levels, provided the U.S. Federal Reserve does what everyone expects and raises interest rates by just a quarter point Tuesday," said Andres McKiguan at Velox Traders.
The bolsa's blue-chip Merval index .MERV rebounded 2.6 percent last week to end Friday at a two-week high of 730.41 points.

Traders said the recovery picked up steam Thursday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan spoke in Congress and hinted strongly at the need for a small, temporary rate hike to ward off inflationary pressures.
Chilean stocks are seen bullish this week as figures showing lower-than-expected economic growth in January fuelled hopes of a reduction in local interest rates.
Chile's central bank trimmed rates last month and officials have said the cuts will continue in coming months provided economic growth is firmly under control.
Last week, the blue-chip .IPSA index lost 2.71 percent to 112.92 points.

In Brazil, shares will take their cue from the Fed's decision in very thin turnover, as stock exchanges will be open only three days this week. Brazilian bourses will close Thursday and Friday for the Easter break.
Last week, the Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most liquid stocks fell 2.0 percent, closing Friday at 9,302 points.
Volatility is likely to set the tone of the Mexican bolsa ahead of the Fed meeting and the Easter holidays, analysts said.
Mexican shares closed up 1.31 percent last week.
Venezuelan stocks were seen headed into a quiet week as investors and brokers cut out to the beach ahead of the Easter break.
"It's like this every year," said one broker. "Few investors, few brokers, and lazy trade."

The 19-share .IBC index closed off 1.7 percent Friday at 6,276.14 points after a week of lackluster trade, despite an historic and unexpected agreement between government, union and private sector leaders to reform the country's social security system.
The agreement is seen paving the way for the country's long-awaited restructuring of the bloated 1.2 million worker state sector.
